name: reading-pleasure
prompt: Reading pleasure: how much a reader would enjoy the act of reading this — voice, wit, craft, momentum — independent of anything taken away from it.

name: mistake-prevention
prompt: Mistake prevention: how likely a reader who never reads this ends up making a specific costly decision or holding a specific false belief that this text would have prevented.

name: challenge-to-priors
prompt: Challenge to priors: how much a reader who currently disagrees with the central claim would be forced to update or sharpen their view after reading it — the text as the strongest opposing case, not merely new information.

name: reader-empowerment
prompt: Reader empowerment: the reader finishes more capable — holding a tool, a move, or a distinction they can apply — rather than merely informed, entertained, or alarmed.

name: misleading-if-trusted
prompt: Misleading if trusted: the chance that a reader who takes this text at face value ends up confidently wrong — through its framing, its omissions, or certainty it has not earned — regardless of how careful it looks.

name: source-uniqueness
prompt: Source uniqueness: how hard it would be to get this text's payload anywhere else — first-hand data, direct experience, or a synthesis no other single text provides — as opposed to content many other texts also deliver.
